note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent judge, after 4c41f84038, which replaced childPolicyParams with childPolicies: one inbound and one outbound policy per negotiated pair, all bound to the one SA, plus inboundStateSelector for the transport-mode state). RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "Thus, a user or administrator MUST be able to order the entries to express a desired access control policy." Prior verdict enforced. The tagged units changed only by childPolicyParams(x, dir) becoming childPolicies(x, dir)[0]; their fixtures carry no selector set, so childPolicies returns exactly one policy and [0] is the same SPParams as before. childPairPolicy resolves Priority from child.PolicyPriority (zero to PriorityChildSA) for every pair, so a multi-pair Child SA carries the operator's rank on every policy. Assertions unchanged: operator rank reaches both directions and orders overlapping peers; unstated order is not 0 and a rekey keeps the default rank; an order capturing IKE is refused (engine and ipsec). All PASS at HEAD. Verdict stands. Owed by the author: the revert record on TestSpdOperatorOrdersOverlappingPeers names childPolicyParams and no longer verifies (unit-changed); re-record it on childPolicies.
